one_liner: Ecwid has a broad REST API (OAuth2 for public apps, static secret tokens for custom apps), but only stores on paid plans can use it; free test-store upgrades are available by emailing support.
auth_notes: External/public apps use OAuth 2.0 to get a non-expiring per-store access token. Custom apps get a secret token and a public token directly from the app dashboard. Native apps get the token through an encrypted payload.
access_notes: The docs say only stores on paid plans can access the API. Developers can email Ecwid for a free plan upgrade on a test store. Calls outside the plan return 402 NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_CURRENT_PLAN.
blocker_notes: The API requires a paid Ecwid plan on the store. A developer test store can get a free upgrade by emailing API support, and each customer's store also needs a paid plan.

evidence.quote: Ecwid uses OAuth 2.0 to provide secure access to the store data for public apps.
Access tokens authorize REST API requests for the specific app in the specific store.
Secret token** grants full REST API access (provided the app has all required permissions) and therefore must be kept safe.
